title: Tenant cooldown orchestrator and usage-credit smoothing
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: tenants with bursty workloads were triggering frequent autoscaler oscillations and emergency burst allocations. Root cause analysis showed short-lived spikes exhaust per-tenant burst tokens then immediate cool-downs which cause repeated headroom provisioning. This PR introduces a Tenant Cooldown Orchestrator (TCO) that centralizes per-tenant cooldown state, exposes adjustable smoothing windows for usage-credit accrual/decay, and provides an oscillation dampener to avoid thrash during transient noise.

What this change does: adds a new orchestrator component in the autoscaler plane that: 1) maintains tenant-level cooldown epochs, 2) smooths burst-credit consumption using an exponential moving average with configurable half-life profiles, 3) integrates with the existing reservation allocator to apply soft-grace periods before triggering cluster-wide onramp, and 4) emits detailed telemetry (cooldown_state, credit_balance_smoothed, dampening_events) for fairness and postmortem analysis.

Design highlights: the orchestrator lives as an independent reconciler (pkg/autoscaler/cooldown_orchestrator.go) and interacts with the existing tenant ledger via a compact RPC surface (in-process in Dedicated). We provide safe defaults and a feature-flag gated rollout. Two smoothing profiles are included: conservative (long half-life for bursty analytic jobs) and responsive (short half-life for interactive workloads). The orchestrator applies a bounded backoff multiplier to repeated onramp requests to prevent repeated controller-triggered increases.

Config and rollout: new config keys under configs/defaults/tenant_policies.yaml (tenant_policies.cooldown.{profile,half_life_sec,max_backoff}) and a helm value helm.redwood.autoscaler.cooldown.enabled (default: false). Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters, start with metric-only (no-enforce) mode for one week, then opt-in enforcement via feature flag per deployment.

Testing and benchmarks: added unit tests for smoothing math and state transitions; integration test simulating 100 tenants with synthetic microbursts (tests/integration/test_cooldown_policy.py). Benchmark run on a five-node dev fleet showed 37% reduction in repeated headroom allocations under the synthetic burst workload and 12% lower overall provisioning cost during the 30-minute test window.

Backward compatibility: when disabled or feature-flag off, no behavior changes. The orchestrator honors existing tenant reservation and burst-token semantics; no schema changes to persisted on-disk ledgers.

Notes: tied to ENG-9182 for follow-up telemetry dashboards (SLOs) and PM-431 for product policy defaults.

Nadia suggested adding a defensive quota check to avoid negative credit balance races; implemented in allocator_integration.go and added unit tests. Liam requested stress tests for 1k tenant churn — added a scaled simulator and posted results in the PR thread. One CI integration run was flaky (timeout on simulator); rerun passed. Ravi asked for clearer observability labels and warned about metric cardinality — adjusted metrics to use low-cardinality enums. Final approvals from Nadia and Liam after addressing tests and telemetry.

Disabled by default; enable via helm value and feature flag. Includes telemetry for cooldown state and credit balances.
